name: Why does a drywall patch sometimes show through the paint, and how is that avoided?

mainEntity.name: Why does a drywall patch sometimes show through the paint, and how is that avoided?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visible flashing occurs when joint compound or texture absorbs paint differently than surrounding drywall, creating dull or shiny spots. To prevent this, the repaired section must be lightly sanded flush, thoroughly dusted, and sealed with a high-quality drywall primer-sealer before the finish coat goes on. In rooms with strong natural light across Denver, Centennial, and Parker homes, applying two topcoats across the entire wall face rather than just over the patch guarantees a uniform sheen and seamless blend.
acceptedAnswer.description: Patches show through when unsealed compound absorbs paint unevenly. Sealing with quality primer and painting the entire wall face prevents visible flashing and sheen mismatch.
